title: FTB question - accelerated closing date
key_point: Scottish closing date brought forward hours after viewing; advice: appoint solicitor before viewing, Home Report replaces survey.

title: Why aren't we getting more viewings? Honest feedback welcome
key_point: Bicester 4-bed townhouse cut £425k to £400k; unclear parking, bare garden, semis/detached competition blamed for low viewings.

title: FTB: What would you offer for this flat?
key_point: Same-block sale £280k, asking £285k after a year; respondents suggest £260-270k citing cooled market, time on market.

title: Home improvements translating into value?
key_point: Glasgow-area buyer paid 10% over Home Report; loft with building warrant adds value, removing parking hurts, street ceiling prices.

title: Bungalow proving to be a niche property
key_point: Belfast 2-bed bungalow with steps fails downsizer criterion; advice to cut price rather than add ramps.

title: Maintenance and running costs for a larger, older house
key_point: Surrey 240sqm solid-wall EPC D home; split views on heating costs; woodwork £10k+, gutters, listing status.

title: Move now or wait until 2030? Family of 5 needing more space
key_point: Family upsizing criteria: home office, bigger garden, extension potential, near family; secondary catchments flagged by respondents.

title: Valuing School Quality Using Boundary Discontinuities (SERC DP18)
key_point: England boundary discontinuity: one SD rise in school value-added or prior achievement raises house prices about 3%.

title: Expectation Adjustment in the Housing Market: Insights from the Scottish Auction System
key_point: Aberdeen sealed bids: premium over asking under 5% (1995-2001), ~35% peak 2007; asking prices sticky, bids volatile.

title: The Amenity Value of English Nature: A Hedonic Price Approach (SERC DP74)
publisher: LSE SERC / Environmental and Resource Economics
key_point: 1m English sales: +1pp ward share of gardens/green space/water raises price ~1% (~£2,000); National Park ~5%.

title: Information transparency and pricing strategy in the Scottish housing market
publisher: International Journal of Housing Markets and Analysis (Lo et al.)
key_point: Abstract only: after Home Report, Aberdeen asking prices tracked comparables more; artificially low asking prices dwindled.

title: Valuing school quality using boundary discontinuities (JUE version)
key_point: Published version of SERC DP18; read via open discussion paper instead.

title: Home Reports - a model to follow?
key_point: Scottish agents: Home Report makes market value transparent; criticisms on lender rejection, 3-month staleness, seller cost.

title: Somerset, Manchester and Salisbury (regional report)
key_point: Manchester demand for big houses, bigger gardens, home working; Salisbury agents overvalue to win instructions; best-and-final common.

title: West Yorkshire, Dorset and Dartmoor (regional report)
key_point: Ripponden buyers prioritise gardens, garages, parking, M62 access; South-East leavers seek lifestyle, family proximity.

title: Northern Ireland (regional report)
key_point: NI average ~£165k, 5-6% growth; 14% buyers returning, citing schools, WFH, family support; negative equity appraisals ended.

title: Northern Ireland is UK's hottest market, claims leading property group
key_point: NI prices +7.5% in 2025 vs UK 2.4%; average £195,936; value, schools, scenery cited.

title: Three out of five homes not selling, reports Zoopla
key_point: Overpriced homes sit; 5% rates add £232/month London FTB vs £66 North East; North regions growing.

title: Manchester fastest, London slowest - north south divide in house prices
key_point: Ten-year growth Manchester 63% vs London 7%; lower starting prices left more room for growth.

title: Town and City Tracker: Manchester lows and Belfast highs
key_point: Manchester -4.2% (Land Registry) vs Belfast +7.6% (Hometrack); only 12 of 30 cities beat inflation since 2005.

title: The commuter belt is widening, says new survey
key_point: 92% of hybrid workers accept longer commute for desired home; 43% add 15-29 min, 32% add 30-44 min.

title: Highest ever values recorded in Scottish property market
key_point: Scotland average £198k, 104,408 sales; ten-year Glasgow +57%, Aberdeen -29%, semis +50%.

title: Scottish housing market 'much stronger' than rest of UK
key_point: Scotland +5.9% to £191,927 vs E&W +3.1%; East Lothian £297k highest, Inverclyde £113.7k lowest.

title: Getting into an oversubscribed school is becoming easier - for now
key_point: 71% of primaries met all first-choice applicants 2025/26; London 15 closures since 2024; school premium pressure easing.

title: Period drama: what age of property commands the highest prices?
key_point: Georgian £531/sqft, 2020s £511, 1920-30s £507; London holds 28.5% of Victorian stock.

title: What we've learnt from Scotland's rental system
key_point: Scottish rent caps: fewer in-tenancy rises (28% vs 53%), new-let rents +8.2%, listings -39% by March 2023.

title: Housing affordability in England and Wales: 2025
key_point: Price/earnings: England 7.6, Wales 6.0, London 10.6, North East 5.0; K&C 25.2; Hull, Hyndburn 4.1.

title: Housing affordability in England and Wales: 2024
key_point: England 7.7, London 11.1, Wales 5.9; only 27 LAs (9%) under 5x earnings.

title: Private rental affordability, England, Wales and Northern Ireland: 2024
key_point: Rent/income: England 36.3%, London 41.6%, North East 19.8%, NI 25.3%; Bristol, Brighton, Watford least affordable outside London.

title: Making an offer (Buying a home in Scotland)
key_point: Solicitor notes interest; multiple notes trigger closing date; offers by solicitor letter; binding at concluded missives.

title: Home Report (Buying a home in Scotland)
key_point: Home Report: single survey with valuation, 16-topic property questionnaire, EPC; seller provides within nine days.

title: House Price Index: September 2026
key_point: North West +3.1%, Scotland +2.6%, London -1.0%; ~75% Scottish homes sell within 3 months vs ~30% London.

title: Rental Market Report: September 2026
key_point: UK rent £1,343, ex-London £1,097; Scotland and England see fewer rentals and higher rental growth.
